subject: Biotechnology
title: Enzymatic Computing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Enzymatic Computing.

hook.text: Enzymes process molecules like CPUs process data — enzymatic computing uses biochemical reactions for parallel processing.

buildup.text: DNA strand displacement reactions compute without cells — synthetic DNA molecules interact to perform calculations in solution.

discovery.text: Neural networks built from DNA can classify molecular patterns — recognizing cancer biomarkers directly in a test tube.

twist.text: Molecular computers are extraordinarily slow — reactions take minutes versus nanoseconds for silicon. Speed is not their strength.

climax.text: Molecular computing excels where silicon fails — operating inside cells, in blood, or at interfaces where electronics cannot go.

punchline.text: Compute with chemistry — enzymatic computing works where silicon chips cannot reach.

quiz.question: Where does molecular computing have an advantage over silicon chips?
options: It processes data millions of times faster than electronic computers
It operates inside living cells, in blood, and at biological interfaces where electronics cannot function
It uses less electricity than any silicon processor
